visual_findings: All nine six-page contact sheets were actually viewed separately, followed by all16 selected detailed pages. Rendering alone received no credit.

Figure6.1/page343 shows percentage reporting an ideal of more than one sex partner next month across regions, not a mean number of partners or actual behavior. Figure6.2/page346 has a probability title but a -3 to+3 likelihood-rating axis; elapsed-time categories run from5years to1hour and are not a linear time axis.

Figure6.3/page348 illustrates the forced choice of revealing face versus body information; its caption continues page349. It is not a result-frequency graph or an individual fertility test. Figure6.4/page368 shows paired edited face/limbal-ring illustrations, not individual medical evidence.

Table6.1/pages355-356 groups behavioral,physiological and psychological clues. Table6.2/pages359-360 lists five classes of hypothesized benefits, includes one1991 personal-communication attribution, and is not a table showing all hypotheses confirmed.

Page371 actually prints r=+51 in both extracted text and enlarged page; adjacent correlations are decimal values. This out-of-range correlation is recorded as an unresolved source numeric issue, not silently repaired to+.51. Page373 reports r=+.55 for ratings versus self-reported SOI in24women, not55percent classification accuracy; several commonly assumed cues are explicitly invalid in that task.
Selected pages369,375,380-381 retain failed-replication/context/genetic-alternative qualifications. Summary language must not erase the qualifications in the chapter body.

Figure7.1/page402 is a reproduced fMRI response-to-child-morphs image; not a paternity,affection or deception test. Photographs on392,397,404,414,428 are illustrations; the page404 broad caption does not replace the selected55-man sample described page403.

Figure7.2/page408 is registered abuse victims per1000children in Hamilton,Ontario1983. Figure7.3/page410 is homicide victims per million child-years of parent-child coresidence in Canada1974-1983; age bins differ from Figure7.2. Relative differences are not absolute probabilities.

Figures7.4/page418 and7.5/page419 use homicides per million children per year, with different vertical scales and nonmonotone small-age movements. Overall age patterns are not strict year-by-year laws; zero in the historical sample does not imply universal zero risk.

Figures7.6/page423 and7.7/page425 use infanticides per million births, not child-years or percentages. The older-age reversal and page424 very small older-case count remain visible; marital-status associations are not current individual causal diagnoses.

Pages413,416-417,421 preserve counterconditions, a seven-twin-pair sample, resource-dependent reversal, and inconclusive Trivers-Willard findings. Parent-offspring numerical example431-432 and Box7.1/pages438-439 were visually checked; toy payoffs and selected historical homicide cases are not a moral ranking of relatives.
